chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me, he said: al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi narrated to me, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), who said:
God, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Dawud (peace be upon him): Indeed, a servant from among My servants may come to Me with a good deed, and I will grant him My Paradise.
He said: So Dawud (peace be upon him) said: O my Lord, and what is that good deed? He said: He brings happiness into My believing servant, even if by giving him a date.
He said: So Dawud (peace be upon him) said: It is right that one who recognizes You should never lose hope in You.

key_terms.الحسنة: Good deed (hasanah); in this context, a single virtuous act that earns Paradise
key_terms.جنتي: My Paradise; God refers to Paradise as His own, signifying divine ownership and bestowal
key_terms.رجاء: Hope (raja'a); in Islamic spirituality, hopeful expectation of God's mercy
key_terms.سرورا: Happiness, joy, delight; the specific act identified as the good deed

ai.seo_question: What good deed earns Paradise according to Prophet Dawud in Islamic tradition?
ai.summary: In this qudsi (divine) narration transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (AS), God reveals to Prophet Dawud (AS) that bringing joy to a fellow believer -- even through the smallest gesture like offering a date -- is a deed worthy of Paradise. The hadith was narrated in the assembly of Sheikh al-Saduq on the last day of Rajab 368 AH. For the original audience of Shia scholars and students, this teaching emphasized that divine mercy is vast and that seemingly small acts of kindness toward fellow believers carry immense spiritual weight.
